traits.stem_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Ariocarpus: plants erect, unbranched, deep-seated in the substrate. Roots taproots. Stem unsegmented, gray-green (yellow-green or purplish with age or stress), above-ground portion flat, concave, or weakly hemispheric, usually flush with soil surface and cryptic, strongly tuberculate, 0-2(-10) × [3-]5-10(-15) cm, hard, rigid, tough skinned; tubercles arranged in rosettes or mosaics, ± triangular, 8-20 × [3-]11-25 mm, hard, exposed faces of tubercles strongly differentiated from sides, prominently fissured [wrinkled, roughened, or nearly smooth]; areoles elongate, forming a wide woolly groove on each tubercle; areolar glands absent. Spines absent. Flowers diurnal, borne in axils of tubercles near stem apex, broadly funnelform to almost salverform, 1.5-5 × 1.5-5 cm; outer tepals brownish or greenish with pink tinge; inner tepals pink or magenta, 13-34 × 4-10 mm; ovary smooth (scales, hairs, and spines absent); stigma lobes 5-10, white. Fruits indehiscent, white or cream to pale greenish, spheric to clavate or cylindric, proximally or almost completely buried in copious wool of stem apex, 10-25 × 5-10 mm, scales and spines absent. Ariocarpus fissuratus var. fissuratus: plants protruding above ground 0-2(-10) cm. Stems: tubercles forming coarse mosaic, closely packed, exposed faces of tubercles deltoid to hemispheric, deeply fissured on either side of central areolar groove, coarsely rugose, often sharply angled apically; areoles to 3 mm wide, sometimes confined to middle of tubercle faces instead of extending to tips. Flowers 2.5-5 cm diam., 2 times wider than long when fully expanded; inner tepals 21-30 × 5.5-7.5(-10) mm. Flowering Sep-Nov. The stems are normally flush with the soil surface and resemble limestone chips in shape, color, and texture. The areoles stand about two thirds of a tubercle's width apart, the plates overlapping in the mosaic; the grey-green of a limestone chip by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from the flora's words: one flat, hard top flush with the soil, sunk to within a centimetre of it, a few magenta flowers from the wool at its centre in autumn. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A rough stem height, most of it below ground: about 4 cm by 30 years. Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: Tubercle width by eye for the 'closely packed' mosaic; a thin woolly cap by eye for the 'copious wool of stem apex' the fruits sit in, its felt a pale tan.

taxon.note: Scientific names as WCVP v16 accepts them, common names as the Flora of North America gives them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
